thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: ingress-proxy-euc2 reported sustained 5xx rate > 12% for 3m. Auto-runbooks: /runbooks/ingress/5xx-euc2. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-0421 :rotating_light:

alex: I'm on the page. seeing a big jump in 502/504 from the envoy fleet in euc2b.

Priya: Grafana snapshots: errors spiked at 21:04 UTC. Latency also up. Most errors originate from envoy->backend TLS handshake failures.

Jamie: copying logs from envoy on a flipped host:
```
[2026-03-15T21:03:58Z] envoy upstream reset peer reset reason=RST_STREAM, connection_id=3421
[2026-03-15T21:04:02Z] upstream response 502 route: /v1/generate
```

oncall-ops: @alex @Priya tagging network team — do we see load balancer healthcheck failures or target group flaps?

alex: ALB target groups show marked increase in unhealthy checks in AZ euc2b, but NLB health looks stable. Could be an AZ-level network impairment affecting some envoy nodes.

Priya: Running quick diff of route53 latencies and AS path anomalies. Preliminary: elevated packet loss on a subset of euc2b NICs. No DNS TTL spike.

Jamie: Temporary mitigations: 1) increase ingress replica count in euc2b to spread load, 2) shift small percentage of traffic to euc1 as a soft failover via routing policy. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

alex: Agree on gradual shift. I'll execute a weighted route change (10% -> euc1) and watch error rate. Also kicking a rolling restart for the worst envoy pods.

Priya: Command I ran to screen pods:
```bash
kubectl -n ingress get pods -o wide | grep euc2b | sort -k6
```
Affected pod IDs: ingress-envoy-7f8c, ingress-envoy-9b2d (restarts increasing).

incident-bot: Action log: alex set routing policy to split 90/10 (euc2:euc1) at 21:08 UTC. oncall-ops initiated restart of 2 envoy pods at 21:09 UTC.

oncall-ops: After the restart error rate dropped to ~6% within 2 mins for the restarted nodes, but others still noisy. Packet drops correlate with euc2b rack r-14.

Jamie: Can we put the rack into maintenance and drain traffic off those hosts? If the cloud provider has a known fabric event we should escalate.

alex: Opening cloud ticket and asking for NIC replacement. Meanwhile increasing the split to 70/30 to reduce user impact. Monitoring customer-facing SLI: request success rate went from 88% -> 96% after shifts.

Priya: Noting partial customer impact: some requests to large context generation timed out (~1.5% of paid requests) between 21:02-21:12 UTC. Logged affected customer ids for outreach.

incident-bot: Severity updated to Sev2 at 21:14 UTC. Pager rotations: Priya -> oncall-ops.

oncall-ops: Cloud provider confirms a noisy NIC fabric in euc2b; they recommended drain and reprovision affected hosts. They've scheduled replacements; ETA 45m.

Jamie: Plan: keep split at 70/30, continue draining bad hosts, no global failover. Postmortem owner: Priya. Communication: ops to draft status update for customers in the incidents page.

alex: I'll hold until provider confirms replacements. Reassigning small followups to SRE runbook tasks.

Priya: Adding eval hooks to Redwood Optimize to catch any latent quality regressions from partial model reroutes.

incident-bot: Incident thread pinned. Next update in 15m or on major changes. :white_check_mark:
